paper.citation: Hartford, J., Lewis, G., Leyton-Brown, K. and Taddy, M. (2017). Deep IV: A Flexible Approach for Counterfactual Prediction. ICML, PMLR 70:1414-1423.
paper.source_version: ICML 2017 published PMLR PDF; author code at commit 349cf027d821d92754ab35ad49320ecf6dfd1c55
paper.source_locator: Published PDF p. 6, Section 4.1, simulation equations; experiments/data_generator.py lines 80-140 for psi, uniform customer type, rho=0.8 and code normalization.

mechanism.name: IV: DeepIV raw-unit demand with endogenous continuous price

generation_equations.expression: T~Uniform(0,10); S~DiscreteUniform({1,...,7}); Z,V,W iid Normal(0,1), mutually independent

sampling.dependence: iid individuals; exogenous random draws mutually independent within individual except explicitly shared latent errors

assumptions: Consistency and no interference; iid individuals.
Instrument Z is independent of T,S,V,W; exclusion: Z enters Y only through price P.
E[e|T,S,Z]=0 because e=rho*V+sqrt(1-rho^2)*W with independent centered normals.
Relevance holds for almost every T: d E[P|T,Z]/dZ=psi(T), whose zeros have probability zero under continuous T.

Identification uses the additive structural-error conditional-moment model, nonzero Gaussian location shifts almost everywhere, and an appropriate regularity/completeness class; arbitrary IV problems are not automatically identified.

properties.notes: Baseline covariates T,S; S is a seven-level category. Price P is endogenous treatment and Z is instrument, neither counted as baseline dimension. S*psi(T)*P is an interaction; quartic and Gaussian bump make psi nonlinear. n=128,d=2 is not high-dimensional.

estimand.name: theta_IV = E[Y(do(P=21))-Y(do(P=20))]
estimand.definition: Population structural mean contrast of a one-unit price intervention, averaging independent T~Uniform(0,10) and S~DiscreteUniform(1,...,7); nuisance latent errors retain their marginal distribution.

truth.expression: Population structural mean contrast of a one-unit price intervention, averaging independent T~Uniform(0,10) and S~DiscreteUniform(1,...,7); nuisance latent errors retain their marginal distribution.
truth.derivation: Closed-form integration over T and seven equally likely customer types; independent Gauss-Legendre integration of both intervention means at orders 64 and 128.

adaptations: Use the main-paper raw-unit equations including the +100 intercept; do not use author-code price/outcome normalization. Author code omits +100 and scales the structural mean before adding error, so this is not an exact code reproduction.
Use S uniform on {1,...,7}, independently of T, as specified in author code; store S as a numeric category instead of seven one-hot columns. rho=0.8 is the author-code default.

Collect a scalar population structural contrast E[Y(do(P=21))-Y(do(P=20))] instead of fitting the complete response surface. This is a continuous-treatment IV contrast, not a binary ATE or a regression conditional on observed P.
Use a local NumPy PCG64 stream and n=128, seed=1729 for interface checking; distributional reconstruction only, with no estimator fitting.
